parsed.explanation: The dossier documents no visitor-facing exposure: no trans-specific criminal offence, no facility or custody rule, no police targeting, no border friction beyond unspecified federal screening that the record does not describe as restrictive. Positives are documented as in force — a human-rights statute expressly covering gender identity (which the visitor can invoke) and a court-established right to marry. Negatives are evidentiary gaps rather than harms: no enforcement record under the statute, no violence data, no documented social acceptance, and the trans-student protection resting on an interpretation rather than a ruling. Those gaps withhold a higher score but do not themselves constitute exposure. Absent any documented tier-1 or tier-2 feature, and with a functioning protective statute on the books, the profile sits in the reduced-risk band.
